sun.upright:
An Aries Sun wants to get there first and be known as the one who did. Fair enough. Mercury, the planet behind The Magician, holds no particular rank in Aries. It's a visitor, and a visitor picks up the habits of the house, and this house belongs to Mars. So what you get from the card is the skill with the speed turned up. Quick words, decisions made on the stairs, a plan that gets worked out while you're already doing it.

The trouble is that Aries has its own card, The Emperor, and he gets his way by telling people. The Magician gets his by laying the tools out and picking one on purpose, and I've noticed Aries Suns find that almost physically annoying. From the inside it feels like being asked to wait about one breath between wanting something and going for it, and that breath feels like a hand on your chest. You'll also know the flip side, the flat, slightly cheated feeling an hour after you've won a point, when you realise you never said what you actually wanted, only what would beat the other person. Mercury as Mars's guest is very good at winning and hazy about what for.

At work this is the person who's pitched three things before the meeting has an agenda, gets two of them, and then discovers nobody wrote down who's doing what. In a relationship it's the argument that ends in ninety seconds with you having said the sharpest true thing, and your partner still quiet about it two days on. With money it's the gear for the project, ordered before the project has a shape. Try this on the next thing you launch. Say in a sentence what it's for, out loud, before you start. If the sentence won't come, you're not ready, whatever the adrenaline is telling you.
sun.reversed:
When this card lands upside down for an Aries Sun, it usually feels like speed with nothing at the end of it. Mercury as Mars's guest gets pushed into talking before it's finished thinking, so you announce the project, you win the argument, you send the message, and then there's no second step behind the first one. Pride makes it hard to go back and check. The ability is there, I'm not doubting that. It's just being spent in bursts that don't add up to anything you can point at.

At work it's the idea that was yours, said too early and too loud, and then picked up by somebody slower who finished it. At home it's the promise made on Saturday morning with real feeling and forgotten by Sunday. Have a look at what you've started lately and ask which of it you'd still want if nobody had seen you begin. Then finish one of those, quietly, without telling anyone until it's done.

moon.upright:
Under all the front, an Aries Moon needs to act on a feeling the second it turns up, because sitting with it feels like being held down. The Magician comes into this sign as a guest. Mercury has no standing in Aries, it just takes on the colour of a hot, cardinal host. What that gives you is a quick tongue for your own moods. You can say what you're feeling almost as fast as you feel it, and for you, saying it counts as doing something, which is why it calms you down.

The problem is that at Aries speed the naming comes out as a blast. 'I'm furious' is true for about ten minutes, and then it isn't, and everyone else in the room is still holding it. From the inside that's baffling. You've moved on, you're fine, you'd like lunch, and the people around you are behaving as if something happened. Something did. What you need is already there, to be honest. It's the second sentence, the one that turns up once the heat has dropped, and it's usually smaller and truer than the first. 'I'm furious' becomes 'I felt left out', and that one can actually be answered.

With a partner this looks like the text sent while you were still hot, and the long quiet afternoon after it. With a parent, especially one who never let you be angry, it's the flare-up that's really about something from twenty years ago. Sleep is where the leftover goes, you lying there arguing with people who've gone to bed. Wait for the second sentence next time. Say the first one to yourself in the car, or the bathroom, and bring only the second one back into the room.
moon.reversed:
An Aries Moon with The Magician the wrong way up is usually restless and can't say about what. Mercury, staying in Mars's house, turns inwards and starts picking fights with you instead. Sharp self-talk. Comebacks rehearsed for arguments that finished days ago. Plans drafted at midnight and gone by breakfast. The urge to act is all still there, it's just that nothing seems worth lighting the match for, so the fire goes into being irritable with whoever's nearest.

Housemates and partners get the worst of it, the snapped answer over nothing, and then you feel terrible and can't explain why you did it. Work gets a burst of energy on Monday and a flat, bored Thursday. What helps is small and physical. Find a ten-minute job you can finish with your hands today, finish it, and let your body notice that something you started actually got done. Do it again tomorrow. The mood usually lifts before the third one.

rising.upright:
Aries rising goes in head first. People read you as direct, quick off the mark, a bit impatient with the preamble. The Magician drawn here adds Mercury to that entrance, and there's some real help in the chart for it. Gemini, Mercury's home sign, sits two signs from Aries, which is a sextile, an easy opening you still have to use. Air feeds fire, and people are getting both from you at once, the push and the patter. You walk in, see what's on the table and you're already using it before the introductions are done.

That works, and it opens doors. It can also flatten a room. Mars as the host wants a result now, and a Mercury working for Mars will supply whatever words get there fastest, and those aren't always the truest ones. From your side it doesn't feel like pushing. It feels like being helpful, getting to the point so everyone can go home. What you don't see is the half-second where the other person decided to keep their own idea to themselves because yours was already in the air. Strangers agree with you and only later wonder what exactly they agreed to.

In a job interview this is the candidate who's answered before the question finished, and got the job, and then found the role wasn't what they'd assumed. In a new friendship it's you organising the second meet-up before the first one's over, which some people love and some quietly back away from. With a tradesperson or a landlord it's a deal struck fast that one more question would have improved. So it's worth asking, when you start something with a new person, whether they've seen what you can actually do or just how quickly you talk. Ask them one thing about themselves before you pitch anything.
rising.reversed:
Turned over on an Aries Ascendant, this is a start that keeps misfiring. You come in strong and it lands wrong. Too blunt, too quick, heard as a pitch when you meant it as an offer. Mercury answering to Mars can make first contact feel like a contest, and the other person may have been bracing lately when you thought they were listening. Or it goes the other way and you hold back the opening move altogether because you don't trust your own delivery.

New colleagues get the clipped version and decide you're difficult before they've had a week to find out you're not. First dates hear a list of what you're looking for and feel interviewed. Either way, try starting the next introduction with a question instead of a statement, and then wait for the whole answer before you say anything else. It'll feel like an age. It's about four seconds.

sun.upright:
A Taurus Sun wants to make something solid and be known for how well it's made. Mercury has no dignity in Taurus, but it isn't a stranger here either, because Virgo, the earth sign Mercury rules, is in trine to yours. Same element, so the two get on. In practice the card's quickness slows down and picks up some taste. All four tools are on your table, but you're the one who lifts each one, feels the weight of it, and decides whether it's any good.

What's going on is a fast planet meeting a fixed sign. Mercury wants to try six things. Taurus wants to do one thing properly. That's useful if Mercury picks the target and Taurus does the staying, and it's a dead end if fixed earth keeps vetoing every new idea as unnecessary, which I've seen happen a lot. From the inside the veto doesn't feel like fear. It feels like good sense. Why change a method that works, why start before you've got the right materials, why rush. Every one of those is a fair question, and if you ask all of them every time, nothing ever reaches the bench.

At work this is the person whose output is excellent and whose range hasn't widened in five years, and who's a bit stung when the promotion goes to someone flashier. With money it's the good, safe earner who's had a side idea for ages and never costed it. In the kitchen or the garden or the workshop, wherever you actually make things, it's the project you've been meaning to start for months. The materials are probably already in the house. Get your hands on them before you've finished thinking it through, and let the first version be a bit rough.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun with this card upside down usually knows exactly what it's capable of and still isn't moving. Mercury living under Venus's roof gets comfortable, and the skill turns into being a connoisseur. You can describe in detail how the thing ought to be done, you can pick apart how other people do it, and your own attempt stays safely unbegun. Fixed earth calls that patience. Often it's really the fear that the finished thing won't match the one in your head.

At work it looks like the reliable pair of hands who's stopped putting ideas forward. At home it's the half-made thing in a drawer, the course paid for and abandoned at week three, the instrument in its case. There's a simple check for this. Is there something one more hour would finish? Give it the hour tonight, and don't judge the result until tomorrow.

moon.upright:
Comfort for a Taurus Moon is physical and it's repeatable. The same mug, the same chair, a full pantry, a body that's been fed. The Magician brings Mercury into that calm as a guest, taking its tone from Venus, so the card's cleverness comes in softened. Your feelings don't especially want analysing. They want handling, the way you'd handle dough or soil.

There's a pull between the two, though. Mercury settles a feeling by putting words on it. A Taurus Moon settles by not having to talk about it at all, and can treat any question as a disturbance of the peace, and your partner or your housemate has probably learned not to ask. From the inside a question like 'are you okay' lands as pressure, as somebody trying to get into a room you'd rather keep shut. You go pleasant and vague and change the subject to dinner. Meanwhile the thing sits there, and fixed earth can sit on a thing for months without it going anywhere. What's being asked for is a bit of both. Say the one plain sentence, then go and do something with your hands.

With a partner this shows up as the week where you're perfectly civil and slightly absent, and they can feel it and can't get a straight answer. With your body it's the appetite that changes when something's wrong, either gone or doubled, well before you'd admit anything's up. And the usual version at home is the practical fix for an emotional problem, reorganising the kitchen the week something's wrong. That's fine. Just make sure the sentence gets said as well, to one person, before the cupboards are done.
moon.reversed:
When The Magician falls reversed on a Taurus Moon, the self-soothing gets overused. Mercury's one foothold in this sign is the decan of the Five of Pentacles, the card of going without, so a rattled mind here goes looking for the purchase, the snack, the small treat that'll fix the mood, and the mood stays because nobody named it. Fixed earth holds feelings a long time, and Mercury the wrong way up won't go and fetch the words.

You might notice yourself telling people you're fine in a very reasonable voice. The bank statement notices before you do, the extra deliveries, the comfort spending. So does your sleep, which gets heavier without getting better. Try this tonight. Put a hand flat on your chest and finish the sentence 'what I actually need is' before you reach for anything else. The first answer is usually 'a biscuit'. Wait for the second.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising comes across as steady and unhurried, somebody who takes their time answering and means it when they do. The Magician puts Mercury on that doorstep as Venus's guest, since it holds no rank of its own in Taurus. The effect on how people are reading you is a quiet sort of competence. You don't pitch. You let people see the work, touch the sample, taste the thing, and that persuades better than talking would.

Where it rubs is that the card wants you to begin, and a fixed earth Ascendant likes to be sure before it moves. Taurus's own card is The Hierophant, who keeps to the tried way, and The Magician makes do with whatever's on the table. From the inside, being asked to move before you're sure feels faintly rude, like being hurried through a meal. You'll say you're thinking about it, and you are, and you'll go on thinking about it in the same careful circle for a fortnight. Openings are turning up that won't wait for you to be certain, and I'd guess at least one has already gone quiet while you thought about it.

In work it's the role someone half-offered you in a corridor that you never followed up because a corridor didn't feel official. In friendship it's the new person who suggested coffee twice and then stopped suggesting. With money it's the good rate that lapsed while you compared it with three others. One small thing to try. Answer the next new invitation within a day, with a yes to the first step only, and nothing beyond that. You can be as slow as you like about step two.
rising.reversed:
First impressions may be working against a Taurus Ascendant here. With the card reversed, Mercury under Venus can read as smooth when you meant it to read as solid. The pleasant manner, the agreeable nod, the 'leave it with me' that then sits there untouched. Strangers take your calm for a commitment and are surprised when nothing follows. Or you're the one being charmed, won over by a good voice and nice presentation.

At work it's the colleague who thinks you agreed to something in a meeting you only nodded through. In buying anything, a car, a course, a kitchen, it's the salesperson who was lovely and the contract you didn't read. Fixed signs hate admitting they were sold something. Before the next yes you give out of politeness, ask yourself whether you'd put a date on it. If you wouldn't, say 'let me come back to you', and then actually do.

sun.upright:
A Gemini Sun is here to stay curious and to be known as the quickest mind at the table. The Magician is Mercury's card and Mercury rules Gemini, which is what's called domicile. The planet's in its own house, strong without straining. So this draw lands on you with the authority of your sign's landlord. It points at what you already do well and says, fine, now do it on purpose.

That last bit is the tension. Mutable air would sooner keep all four tools in the air than put three of them down. Look at the figure on the card, one hand up, one hand down, the idea carried all the way into the ground. That's the choosing part, and it's the part Gemini Suns tend to skip, because pride for you lives in being clever and the card is asking whether you'd also like to be finished. From the inside, choosing one thing feels like a small death of the others. The moment you commit to the podcast, the novel and the business idea start looking better, and you can feel your attention sliding sideways toward them, and it's a relief to let it.

At work this is the person everyone wants in the brainstorm and nobody quite trusts with the delivery, which is unfair and also a little bit earned. In a relationship it's the partner who's wonderful company and a bit hard to plan a life with, because next year keeps changing shape. With a project of your own it's three folders on the laptop, each about a quarter done. Which of your current ideas would you be proud to have your name on in a year's time? Give that one your mornings, and let the other two have the evenings if they must.
sun.reversed:
Mercury at home in Gemini is strong in both directions, so when The Magician reverses for a Gemini Sun the talent doesn't go anywhere, it just slips its lead. This is the trickster end of your ruler. The brilliant explanation for why it isn't done. The version of events tailored to whoever's listening. The five projects that keep you from being judged on any one of them. You can usually talk your way out, and that's the problem.

In a job it's the update that sounds like progress and describes none. With a partner it's the small reshaping of what happened on Saturday so that it's nobody's fault. Listen this week for the moment you hear yourself being persuasive and don't quite believe it. That's the place to stop and say the plainer thing, even if it's 'I haven't started', and let it sit there without a follow-up.

moon.upright:
What a Gemini Moon needs is company for its thoughts. Someone to talk to, something to read, a window open in the mind. Mercury rules Gemini, so The Magician comes in here as the planet that owns the place. Feelings wanting a name is only half of it with this Moon. Naming is how you feel. A mood isn't quite real to you until you've said it to someone, and once you've said it, it often lifts.

Mercury in its own sign is unforced, and that's a genuine gift. You've got unusual access to your own weather and the words for it. What to watch is that mutable air moves on quickly. You can describe a hurt perfectly on the Tuesday and be bored of it by the Thursday, while your body is still carrying it around. From the inside it feels finished. You told the story, people were kind, it made a good story, and the story has replaced the feeling. Then you're short-tempered on Friday and can't think why, and the answer is Tuesday.

With friends this shows up as being the one who's always fine to talk to and rarely the one who's not fine, because by the time anyone asks, you've already narrated it into shape. With sleep it's the mind still talking at midnight, drafting the message, replaying the exchange. With a partner it's the hurt you explained so well that they think it's resolved, and you thought so too. I'd try this. After you've explained how you feel to someone, stay quiet for a full minute, and see what's still there once the words have run out. Say that bit too, even if it's only three words.
moon.reversed:
For a Gemini Moon the reversed Magician is the mind running with nobody at the desk. Mercury is powerful in its own sign, and turned inwards that power becomes chatter. Two voices arguing over every feeling, the phone checked forty times, sleep pushed back by one more tab. You aren't short of insight. There's so much commentary going on that the feeling underneath can't get a word in.

Nervous energy is the giveaway. Friends get long voice notes at odd hours. Work gets a scattered day where you touched everything and finished nothing. Your body gets the skipped lunch and the tight jaw. Give the restless part a job with an end to it, like writing the whole worry out by hand on a single page, and then close the notebook and leave it closed. If the page fills, that's fine. Don't start a second one.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising enters a room mid-conversation. Bright-eyed, hands moving, curious about everyone. Mercury rules this Ascendant, so The Magician is close to a picture of your chart's front door. The card's planet is at home in your rising sign and none of this has to be forced. People are meeting you at your most fluent and they're responding to it. Introductions turn into offers. A passing remark turns into a plan.

Strong isn't the same as settled, though. Gemini's own card is The Lovers, which is about choosing, and The Magician needs a choice too before any of his tools do a thing. A mutable Ascendant can open ten doors in a week and walk through none of them, and I've seen that pattern run on for years. From your side each door feels like it's still open, because you could go back, couldn't you, and the person seemed keen. What you don't notice is how quickly other people's keenness cools when the follow-up doesn't come, and how the reputation for being all talk arrives a good year before anyone says it to your face.

In work it's the contact made at a conference and left in a pocket. In dating it's the great first evening that turns into a fortnight of witty messages and no second date, with both of you waiting for the other one to suggest it. With a project it's the collaborator you've enthused at three times and never sent a single file. The world is taking you at your word, so your word is worth spending carefully. Of all the things you've said 'we should' about lately, pick one and put a date on it before the end of the week.
rising.reversed:
People may be finding a Gemini Ascendant hard to pin down. Reversed, the card takes Mercury's home-ground fluency and makes it slippery, so you get read as charming, quick, and possibly not to be relied on, whether or not that's fair. Mixed messages are likely and some of them are yours. You say yes lightly and the other person hears a contract. There can be a bit of stage fright in it too, the usual patter deserting you at a first meeting.

At work it's the manager who's stopped asking you for estimates because they've learned to double them. In a new friendship it's the plan that was 'definitely' and then wasn't, twice. Slow the opening line down. Say one true thing about why you're there and let the silence after it stand. If you catch yourself about to promise something in the first five minutes, hold it until the last five.

sun.upright:
Protecting what it loves is the life's work of a Cancer Sun, and it wants to be seen as the one who held everything together. Mercury has no special standing in Cancer. It visits, and takes its colour from the sign's ruler, the Moon, so The Magician's skill reaches you through feeling and memory first. Your cleverness is emotional cleverness. Reading the room, knowing what someone needs before they've asked, finding the words that make a person feel safe.

That's real power and the card wants you to use it deliberately, in your own name. Cancer is cardinal, a starting sign, but water starts things sideways, and you can spend the whole of your skill on other people's projects without noticing. From the inside this doesn't feel like hiding. It feels like being needed, which is close to the best feeling there is for this Sun. The trouble comes later, in a quiet moment, when you look at all the things you've helped into being and can't find one with your name on it, and something in you goes tight and a bit resentful, and you're ashamed of the resentment. Mercury borrowing the Moon's memory will then remind you of every time you did put yourself forward and it went badly.

At work it looks like being the person who makes the team function and never the one who presents. With a partner it's knowing exactly what would help their career and having no plan for yours. With a parent, it can be the old family role, the capable one, still running your decisions at forty. So what are you building that's yours? Usually there's a plan you've told nobody about, because saying it out loud feels exposed. Say it to one person you trust, and soon, before you talk yourself out of it.
sun.reversed:
A Cancer Sun knows how to get its way without asking, and the reversed Magician points straight at it. Mercury coloured by the Moon can turn skill with feelings into management of them. The hint instead of the request. The sigh that does the work of a sentence. Care offered with a small hook in it. Usually it comes from being afraid of a flat no. The cost is that nobody gets to meet what you actually want, and that includes you.

With a partner it's the evening you wanted and never asked for, and the silence when they didn't guess. At work it's the credit you'd like and angle for instead of claiming. With a grown child or a parent it's help that arrives with conditions nobody agreed to. Find one place where you've been steering from the side lately, and ask directly for the thing instead. You may well get a yes, and if you get a no it'll be over in a minute.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon is the Moon in the sign she rules, and what she wants is easy to say and hard to get. To feel held, and to know everyone under the roof is all right. The Magician brings Mercury in as a visitor, and since Cancer's ruler is the Moon, the card's planet is answering directly to the thing this placement is. Thinking works for feeling here, never the other way round.

That makes your moods unusually articulate. Memory is handing you words, old scenes are explaining current reactions, and you may find you can finally tell someone what a particular hurt was about. The friction is that Mercury is quick and this Moon is tidal. Explaining a feeling doesn't finish it, and you can't hurry the water, however good the explanation was. From the inside it goes like this. You work out, with real clarity, why a remark upset you, and you feel better for about an hour, and then the same remark washes back in at bedtime as if you'd never understood it at all. That isn't failure. It's what water does, and the understanding still counts.

With a partner this is the conversation that needs having twice, once to explain and once more, a few days later, to be held about it. With your mother or whoever mothered you, it's old scenes surfacing with new captions, and some of those captions are worth saying to them and some aren't. Your body keeps the tally too, the stomach tightening before your mind has caught up. Let the words come and then let the tide do the rest. Write the message, by all means. Send it after you've slept on it.
moon.reversed:
When this card reverses on a Cancer Moon, Mercury stops translating feelings and starts building cases. The Moon rules this sign, so emotion sets the agenda, and a reversed Mercury supplies the evidence. Every slight remembered with its date. A story about what they really meant, rehearsed until it feels like fact. Or the words fail altogether and you go quiet behind the shell hoping to be guessed. Neither one gets you held.

In a friendship it's the three-week silence over something the other person doesn't know they did. At home it's the meal cooked in pointed quiet. The case feels airtight because you've been over it so many times, and that's exactly the problem. Before you act on the story, check one detail of it with the actual person involved. You may be working from a very old script, one that was written about somebody else entirely.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes in sideways, reads the mood of a place before committing to it, and strangers find you gentle, watchful and a bit guarded. Draw The Magician against that and Mercury walks in with no dignity of its own, though it does rule Cancer's middle decan, the Three of Cups, the card of friends raising a glass. So its way into this sign is through company. The card's confidence comes out through your sensitivity, and you're quicker than usual to find the opening line, and it works because it's tuned to whoever you're talking to.

The pull is between the card's readiness and your shell. Cancer's own card is The Chariot, who goes forward in armour. The Magician stands there in the open with his tools out on the table. You're being asked to start things where people can watch you starting them, which a Cancer Ascendant finds faintly indecent. From your side, a public beginning feels like walking into a room with your coat off in winter. You'd rather have a friend introduce you, or a reason to be there, or to have already met everyone once. And the odd thing is that once you're in, you're very good, warmer and funnier than the guarded first minute suggested, and people are surprised by the gap.

In work it's the job you'd be excellent at and won't apply for cold, because cold applications feel like exposure. Socially it's the group you've been invited to twice and haven't gone to yet because you don't know anyone there. In a new romance it's waiting for the other person to say something first, for weeks. Picture an opportunity that needs you to introduce yourself first. Do it while the nerve's there. You can retreat afterwards, that's allowed, and you'll probably find you don't want to.
rising.reversed:
Caution has the upper hand for Cancer rising when the card lands upside down. Mercury taking its cues from the Moon gets changeable at the door. Warm one day, unreachable the next, and new people can't tell which of you they're going to get. You may be testing them before you've shown them anything, or sending signals you think are obvious and they can't read at all.

A new colleague reads the quiet as disapproval when it's shyness. Someone you like reads the retreat after a good evening as loss of interest, and moves on. Chances to start something are passing while you wait to feel safe enough. Safe may not come first. Pick one new contact and tell them plainly what you're hoping for, in a single sentence, and send it before you've reread it more than once.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to be seen doing the thing they're best at, and they want it to be unmistakably theirs. Put The Magician on that and you get a card about performance in the old sense, the showing of a skill. Mercury has no rank in Leo. It's a guest in the Sun's house, and a guest of the Sun ends up lit by it, so the card's cleverness goes into delivery, into whether a thing lands. There's an easy link through Gemini too. Mercury's home sign sits two signs from Leo, a sextile, which is an opening that's there to be used and won't use itself.

Where it rubs is that Leo is fixed fire and likes to be good at one thing for a long time, while Mercury likes to be good at the next thing. So you get caught between the act you've polished and the new idea that's more fun, and pride makes both harder. Dropping the old act feels like admitting it wasn't enough. Starting the new one badly, in front of people, feels worse. I see a lot of Leo Suns only doing what they already know they'll be praised for, and they're a bit bored, and they can't quite say why.

At work it shows up as the presentation you could give in your sleep and the course you haven't signed up for because you'd be a beginner again. In love it's needing your partner to be impressed and feeling oddly flat when they're only pleased. With a child or a younger colleague it can be the skill you'd love to teach and keep doing yourself, because it's quicker and it's yours. Pick one thing you'd like to be good at in two years and be openly bad at it for a month. Tell someone you're learning, so the being bad has an audience you chose.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Sun, The Magician turns into a show. The skill's real, but it's being spent on looking capable, and Mercury lit by the Sun can get very good at the looking. The confident answer to a question you didn't quite follow. The project announced with a lovely logo and no second month. Or the opposite, the pride that won't try anything it might not shine at, which passes for high standards and is mostly a fear of being watched while you fail.

It turns up at work as a reputation slightly bigger than the output, and you can feel that gap even if nobody's mentioned it. With friends it's taking the story over and telling it better than the person it happened to. Choose one piece of work where nobody will see the process. Do it properly, all the way through, and don't mention it until somebody else notices.

moon.upright:
Somebody noticing is what settles a Leo Moon. Being told you did well, being chosen, having the warm attention of a person you love, those are what fill this Moon back up. The Magician comes into Leo as the Sun's guest, with no standing of its own, and it borrows that heat. So you feel in big, clear colours and you've got the words to match. When you're hurt you can say so with real force. When you're happy the whole house knows about it.

The card and this Moon disagree about speed. Fixed fire holds a feeling for a long time, a grudge or a loyalty, and Mercury wants to name it and move along. You'll recognise the evening where you've said exactly what upset you, beautifully, and it's all still sitting there the next morning, because the saying was a performance of the feeling and the feeling itself hasn't been touched. There's pride in it as well. Admitting that a small thing hurt, a forgotten call, a friend's party you weren't asked to, feels beneath you, so you make a bigger and more dignified complaint about something else.

With a partner this is the row about the dishes that's really about not being looked at properly for a week. With friends it's being the generous host and then lying awake counting who didn't say thank you. The body tends to carry it as a heat that won't settle, a flushed face, sleep that comes late. Say the small version out loud to one person. 'I was hurt you didn't ask me' is plenty, and it's much easier for them to answer than the big version.
moon.reversed:
With The Magician reversed, a Leo Moon goes looking for an audience for its feelings and then resents the audience. Mercury under the Sun makes a good story out of every hurt, told well and told often, and the telling slowly takes the place of what actually happened. Or the pride shuts it all down and you go bright and busy and fine, and nobody's allowed near the sore spot, including the people who could help.

Friends notice the story has been told three times, to three people, with small improvements each time. A partner notices you're sunny with everyone except them. Sleep goes, or goes shallow. If one person actually hurt you, tell that person the plain version once, without the flourishes. Then stop telling it to anyone else and see how long the feeling lasts when it isn't being retold.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in like it was expected, and mostly it was. People see warmth, a bit of theatre, somebody who'll make the evening better. The Magician on that entrance puts Mercury, the Sun's guest in Leo, in charge of your delivery. You're quick on your feet, you've got the line that gets the laugh, and the sextile from Gemini to Leo means the wit and the presence help each other along, provided you actually make use of it.

The catch is that Leo rising is fixed, and it likes a reliable act. You know what works with a new crowd and you do it, and it works, and after a while people have met the act a dozen times and still haven't met you. Mercury would sooner improvise. There'll be moments where you feel the familiar line coming, sense it's slightly wrong for this particular person, and say it anyway because it's safe. Strangers love it. The ones who stay around start wondering what's underneath, and some of them stop waiting to find out.

At a job interview this is the charm that gets you through the first round and the harder question in the second round that the charm can't answer. On a first date it's being good company for two hours with neither of you mentioning anything true. In a new team it's being liked quickly and taken seriously slowly. Next time you meet someone new, skip the opening you know works. Ask them something you genuinely want to know and let it be a bit awkward.
rising.reversed:
When The Magician falls reversed on a Leo Ascendant, the first impression can run ahead of the person making it. Big entrance, big promises, the easy confidence that gets you through the door, and then people are waiting for the follow-through the entrance implied. Or the confidence deserts you and you do the act on autopilot, smile on and nobody home, hoping nobody spots the difference.

It shows at work as the pitch that won the client and the colleague who's now stuck delivering it, and who's started to mind. Socially it's being the life of the party and going home feeling oddly unseen, which is a lonely sort of tired. For the next few weeks, promise a little less than you know you can do in any first meeting, and let people be pleasantly surprised by the rest.

sun.upright:
Virgo is the one sign where Mercury both rules and is exalted, so for a Virgo Sun The Magician is about as strong as this card ever gets. Mercury is your sign's ruler, which means the card speaks with the landlord's voice. What a Virgo Sun wants is to be useful and to be good at it, to be the person who can actually fix the thing. This card says you can, and that it's time to do it where people can see you doing it.

The tension comes from Gemini, Mercury's other home, which squares Virgo. Same planet, two moods. Gemini wants to try it and see. Virgo wants to get it right first. A square is friction that forces action, and you'll feel it as a small argument in your head every time you're about to start something, one voice keen to begin and one that's already found the flaw. Exaltation means Mercury is at its most refined here, and refinement is wonderful until it becomes the reason nothing leaves your desk. I've met Virgo Suns with ten years of excellent drafts in a folder.

At work it's the report that's better than anyone else's and a week late. With money it's the careful budget where the one investment in yourself, a course, a proper tool, a day off, keeps missing the cut. Mercury also rules the last ten degrees of Virgo, the decan of the Ten of Pentacles, so for some of you it's family, the family business or the family way of doing things, that's asking for your skill. Send something out at ninety per cent. Pick it deliberately, and notice that nobody else can see the missing ten.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun with this card reversed has all the skill in the world and it's pointed at the wrong target. Usually at you, sometimes at other people. Mercury is very strong in Virgo, strong both ways, and upside down it turns into the critic who never makes anything. The edit on someone else's work, the list of what's wrong with the plan, the private tally of your own mistakes kept going late into the evening. It can feel like being responsible. Mostly it's a way of never being judged yourself.

At work it shows up as fixing a colleague's email while your own project hasn't moved in a month. At home it's the partner who's stopped asking for help because the help comes back with notes. Go one whole day without correcting anybody, yourself included, and put the energy you save into one small thing of your own.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon feels safe when things are in order. The drawer tidied, the plan checked, the body looked after properly. Mercury rules Virgo and is exalted there, so The Magician on this Moon speaks your emotional language exactly. You calm yourself by making sense of things, and by doing something useful with your hands while you work it out. When you're anxious you clean the kitchen, and honestly, it helps.

What gets hard is that Mercury in its sharpest sign can analyse a feeling to pieces. You know precisely why you're upset, you can list the causes in order of importance, and knowing hasn't helped at all. The square from Gemini to Virgo adds a restless edge, a mind that keeps checking, the lock, the tone of a message, the thing you said at dinner. It feels like being careful. It's tiring in a way people around you rarely see, because from the outside you look entirely calm.

The body is often where this lands first. A tight stomach, skin that flares, sleep broken at three with a list running in your head. With a partner it's showing love by sorting out their tax return and never quite saying you were lonely last week. With a parent it's the old habit of being the good, helpful child so nobody gets upset. When you catch yourself tidying for the second time in a day, stop and ask what it's about. Write the answer in one line and leave it unedited.
moon.reversed:
The reversed card on a Virgo Moon is worry with a job title. Mercury at full strength in your sign, turned inwards, audits everything you feel. Was that reaction reasonable, is this tiredness something serious, did your friend mean it that way. There's a great deal of thinking and very little comfort, and the routines that normally settle you start to feel like rules you keep failing.

Sleep shows it first, then digestion, then your patience with the people who love you. A partner might hear the fifth question about the same small thing and not know what to say. Your body gets the rigid version of good habits, the skipped treat, the extra check. Take one routine and deliberately do it badly for a week, the half-made bed, the unplanned lunch, and notice that nothing falls apart.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising looks composed and slightly reserved, the person who clocked your shoes, the typo on the menu and where the exit is. The Magician drawn for your mask brings Mercury home, the planet that rules your Ascendant and is exalted in it, so the way you come across is sharp and credible. People trust you to be accurate. You'll find they hand you the detail, the logistics, the contract to read over before anyone signs.

That's a real asset and it can box you in. The card is about beginning, about picking up the tools, and Virgo rising likes to be ready before it's seen. The Gemini square is where the strain sits, the part of you that'd love to just say the funny thing or pitch the idea half-formed, and the Virgo instinct that edits it first. So what people meet is careful and helpful, and they don't always meet your ideas at all. You come across as the one who checks, which is fine, until you'd like to be the one who's asked.

In a new job this is being given all the admin in week one and still doing it in year three. In a friendship it's being the reliable one and never the one people ring when they want a laugh, though you're genuinely funny. Buying something big, a car or a flat, it's the clause you spotted that saved everyone money and nobody thanked you for. In the next meeting, say your idea before you say your correction. Put the idea first, however rough it is.
rising.reversed:
First contact goes a bit stiff for Virgo rising with The Magician upside down. The accuracy that usually reassures people reads as coolness or fussiness, because Mercury, strong on your Ascendant, is spending its effort on avoiding mistakes instead of on reaching the person in front of you. You might hear yourself correcting someone you've only just met. Or you get so careful you hardly say anything, and they fill the silence with their own guesses about you.

A new manager might take your questions as doubt. A date might take the precision as judgement. Fair or not, that's how it's being received. Loosen one thing on purpose. Let a small mistake stand in a message without fixing it, or tell a story that isn't quite finished, and see whether anyone minds. Usually nobody does.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns want to make things fair and lovely and to be liked while they do it, which is harder than it sounds. The Magician comes into Libra as a guest of Venus, with no special rank, but it's in good company, because Gemini, Mercury's home sign, is trine to Libra. Two air signs, same element, easy flow. Your mind works well with this card. You're persuasive, you see both sides fast, and you can talk two people into agreeing who came in shouting.

The trouble is that The Magician is a card about deciding what you want and doing it, and Libra is the sign that hesitates, because every choice leaves someone out. You'll know the feeling of looking at three good options and wanting all three kept open until everyone's happy. Libra is cardinal, though. It's meant to start things. Your own card is Justice, with the sword and the scales, and weighing is only half of that picture. At some point the sword has to come down, and Mercury in a Venus sign will find very graceful ways to put that moment off.

At work this looks like being the diplomat in every dispute and never quite pushing your own proposal through. In love it's being wonderful at understanding your partner's side and slow to say what yours is. With friends it's the holiday you organised for everybody and didn't enjoy, because nobody asked where you wanted to go. Pick the decision you've been politely stalling on. Make it by a set date, and tell the people it affects kindly and without a long explanation.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with this card reversed is using its charm to avoid being pinned down. Mercury as Venus's guest is lovely company and very good at telling people what they'd like to hear. The trouble is the gap afterwards. The agreement you didn't mean, the favour you'll resent, the opinion you swallowed to keep the evening pleasant. It adds up over months, and people end up liking you a great deal without being sure what you think about anything.

This tends to show up at work as being agreeable in meetings and privately irritated by the outcome. In a relationship it's the resentment that seems to come out of nowhere and has in fact been saved up since the spring. Find one honest thing you've been rounding off to keep the peace. Say it gently, but say the whole of it.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon needs peace, and more specifically it needs the people it loves to be getting on. Discord in the house gets into your body. The Magician arrives here as Venus's guest, and with Gemini trine Libra, air meeting air, the card's gift runs easily for you. You can talk feelings through and make them reasonable. You find the words that let two people come back together, including you and whoever you've fallen out with.

Talking a feeling into something reasonable can also mean talking it out of existence. You're very good at seeing why the other person did what they did, and by the time you've understood them there's nowhere left for your own hurt to go. The card's Mercury is comfortable in air, and air likes an explanation. Your body may not agree. Venus, who rules Libra, wants things to feel right, and a feeling that's been explained away doesn't feel right at all. It just goes quiet and turns up later as a headache.

With a partner it looks like always being the one who makes the first move to smooth things over, and asking for nothing back. With friends it's the peacekeeper role in the group chat, reading every message twice for tone. In your body it can be a heavy tiredness after social things, even good ones, from all that invisible balancing. When you next feel annoyed, let yourself be annoyed for an hour before you start working out why they did it. Their reasons will still be there afterwards.
moon.reversed:
When the card reverses for a Libra Moon, feelings turn into negotiations. Mercury under Venus keeps looking for the fair version, the right tone, the reply that won't upset anyone, and you end up drafting your emotions instead of having them. Or you can't tell what you feel at all, because every feeling seems to need somebody else's approval before it's allowed in the room.

This shows up with a partner as asking what they want for dinner five times and being secretly cross about the answer. With friends it's the message you've rewritten so often it no longer says anything, sitting unsent. With your body it's the tension in the shoulders after a perfectly nice visit. Next time someone asks how you are, give a short answer that's true, and don't soften it with a joke.

rising.upright:
Libra rising arrives graceful and easy to talk to, the one who makes the introductions and remembers everybody's name. The Magician on the Ascendant plays straight into that. Mercury is only a guest in Libra, but Gemini, its home, is trine to your rising sign, so the card's quick talk and your social grace are pulling in the same direction. First meetings tend to go well, and new contacts go home feeling understood.

Libra is cardinal air, a starting sign, and the card wants you to start, but a Libra Ascendant tends to begin by mirroring. You match the other person's tone, their pace, sometimes their opinions, and it works so well you can lose track of what you came in to say. The Magician's table has four tools on it, and you're the one who's meant to pick. What people meet is a very pleasant version of what they already think, unless you bring your own view in early and let it be a bit different from theirs.

In a negotiation this is the deal that felt friendly and left you with less than you wanted. On a first date it's being so tuned in to them that they learn almost nothing about you. In a new job it's being well liked from the first day and consulted on nothing important. Before your next meeting with someone new, decide one thing you want out of it. Get that said in the first ten minutes, however nicely the rest goes.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with The Magician reversed can come across as all surface. Mercury in Venus's sign turns the charm up and the content down, and people leave a first meeting having liked you and unsure what you actually said. You may be giving each person the version of you they'll like best. That's exhausting to keep up, and it tends to catch up with you when two of those people meet.

At work it's two colleagues comparing notes and finding you agreed with both of them. Socially it's the invitations you accepted to be polite and now can't face, and the excuses you're inventing to get out of them. At the next introduction, say something you actually think that the other person might disagree with. Say it calmly, and let them disagree.

sun.upright:
A Scorpio Sun wants to get to the bottom of things and to be known as the one who can't be fooled. The Magician is a visitor here. Mercury has no rank in Scorpio and takes its colour from the sign's ruler, Mars, or Pluto if you work with the modern ruler, so the card's cleverness goes sharp, private and a bit relentless. There's help from Virgo, Mercury's exalted sign, which is sextile to Scorpio. That link gives you precision. You notice the one detail that doesn't fit and you don't let it go.

The strain is between the card's openness and your instinct to keep your cards close. The Magician lays everything out on the table. Scorpio would prefer nobody saw the table. Gemini, Mercury's other home, is quincunx to Scorpio, five signs apart with nothing in common, and that shows up as constant small adjustments between the part of you that wants to say it and the part that decides not to. You'll know it from meetings where you had the answer and held it back to see who else knew.

Professionally you're the researcher, the investigator, the one who reads the whole contract, and sometimes the colleague others find slightly alarming. In love it's knowing your partner's moods better than they do and keeping yours to yourself. With money it's quietly having a plan nobody else has heard about. The card asks you to use that insight in the open for once. Pick one thing you've worked out and share it with the person it'd help most, all of it, holding nothing in reserve.
sun.reversed:
This card reversed on a Scorpio Sun is insight used as leverage. Mercury in Mars's sign gets tactical, and upside down it keeps what it knows for later. The secret held because it might come in useful. The test set for a friend who doesn't know they're being tested. The long silence that makes someone else say too much. It works, often very well, and it leaves you lonely in a way that's hard to admit.

At work it's the information you sat on until it could win you something, and the trust that quietly drained away once people noticed. In love it's a memory for every wrong, filed and dated. Ask yourself what you're keeping in reserve and what it's costing you to keep it. Hand one piece of it over, plainly, to someone who'd be glad to have it.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel everything at full depth and trust very few people with it. What you need is loyalty, privacy and the truth, in roughly that order. The Magician brings Mercury into Scorpio as a guest of Mars, with no dignity of its own, and what it offers is words for the deep water. For a Moon that often feels things too big to say, a card that says you can name it is a lot.

The rub is that Mercury's Gemini side is quincunx to Scorpio, two signs with nothing in common that have to keep adjusting to each other. Light chat and deep feeling don't sit well together, and you'll feel it when someone asks how you are and you can't find any version of the answer that isn't either a lie or far too much. Virgo is sextile to Scorpio, though, and that's the way in. Precise, small, exact words. You don't need to explain everything you feel. You need the one accurate sentence, and you're better at finding it than you think.

With a partner this might be finally saying what one particular silence of theirs does to you. With family it's the old thing nobody talks about, and the relief when one person does. At night it can show as dreams that are unusually vivid, the mind doing its naming while you sleep. Choose the person you trust most and tell them one true thing you've never said out loud. Keep it short. You can say more another day if you want to.
moon.reversed:
When The Magician is upside down on a Scorpio Moon, the words go underground. Mercury in Mars's sign turns inwards and starts plotting, rehearsing and interpreting, reading every message for what's hidden in it. You're certain you know what's going on in someone else's head, and you may be partly right, and you aren't checking.

It tends to show up as a jealousy that can't be argued with, or a silence at home that everyone can feel and nobody names. Sleep goes restless and the three o'clock thoughts get very convincing. Someone you love may be walking carefully around you without knowing why. Ask one direct question about the thing you've been interpreting. Take the answer as given for a week before you decide what it really meant.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising comes across as watchful and hard to read, and people often feel seen before they've said much at all. The Magician drawn here puts Mercury on that doorway as a guest of Mars. It gives you a quiet, sharp confidence at the start of things. You say little, what you do say lands, and you've usually worked out the room before anyone's worked you out.

What pulls against it is that this card is about the open hand, all four tools on show, and a Scorpio Ascendant likes to reveal nothing until it's sure. The Virgo sextile is on your side, the careful, exact use of what you know. The Gemini quincunx isn't, and you'll feel that in small talk, which you find genuinely hard and faintly pointless. So first meetings split. The ones where you decide to show a little go brilliantly. The ones where you stay behind the glass tend to leave people nervous of you, and they won't tell you so.

In an interview this is the answer that's short, exact and slightly unnerving to the panel. In dating it's the intensity people find attractive in the first hour and hard work by the third date if nothing opens up. At a new workplace it's the reputation for being formidable, earned in week one by saying very little. Next time you meet someone, offer one ordinary personal thing early. Your weekend, a book, the town you grew up in. Small, true, and given freely.
rising.reversed:
For Scorpio rising, the reversed card turns reserve into suspicion. Mercury in Mars's sign reads every newcomer for their motive, and people can feel themselves being assessed from the moment they sit down. Or you give off a charge you don't intend, and your silence gets taken for judgement when it's really caution.

It shows at work as new colleagues keeping their distance, and you taking the distance as proof they're hiding something. In friendship it's testing people before you'll let them in, and losing the good ones who don't enjoy being tested. With a new neighbour it's the wave you didn't return. At the next first meeting, say what you honestly think about the conversation you're having, out loud, a bit sooner than feels comfortable.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are here to find out what it all means and to say so, loudly, to anyone who'll listen. The Magician is an awkward guest in your sign. Mercury is in detriment in Sagittarius, the sign opposite Gemini, its home, which means it's working against the grain. Mercury likes the detail, the fact, the exact word. Sagittarius likes the big picture and the sweeping claim. So when this card turns up for you, the skill being asked for is one you have to reach for.

You'll know the feeling. You can see the whole shape of an idea at once, the book, the business, the move abroad, and the moment someone asks about the second step, something in you goes flat. Virgo, Mercury's other sign, squares Sagittarius as well, so planning, checking and admin all feel like friction. And yet there's a foothold. Mercury rules the first ten degrees of Sagittarius, the decan of the Eight of Wands, the card of things flying fast through the air. When Mercury works for you here it works as speed, messages going out, a plan pulled together over one weekend.

In a job you're the one with the best vision in the room and the worst spreadsheet, and a real chance to get the vision taken seriously if the detail gets done. In study it's the course you'd love that has a dull middle module. In love it's the big promise, the trip or the future, made sincerely and never costed. Take the idea you talk about most and write down the next three physical steps, each small enough for an afternoon. Do the first one before you tell anyone else about the idea.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Sagittarius Sun can talk a very good game. Mercury in detriment in your sign, turned over, becomes the sweeping claim with nothing under it. The opinion stated as fact, the plan that's mostly enthusiasm, the story that grows a little every time it's told. You believe it when you say it, which is exactly why other people believe it too, for a while.

At work it shows up as the colleague whose big announcements have started getting a polite nod and no follow-up questions. With friends it's the trip you've all been planning together for three years. In love it's the future you describe beautifully and haven't taken a single step towards. Pick one thing you've said you'll do and either do the first part of it or say out loud that you won't. Either answer clears the air.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. Space to move, something to look forward to, a sense that life is bigger than this week. The Magician is uneasy here. Mercury is in detriment in Sagittarius, so the card's habit of naming and sorting doesn't suit your emotional style, which is to feel a thing hugely, find the meaning in it and get going again. You don't usually want your feelings itemised. You want them understood in one broad sweep.

Gemini sits opposite Sagittarius, and an opposition is a pull toward balance, the same axis seen from its other end. That's the gift in this draw, oddly enough. Gemini's end of the axis is the small, near, particular stuff, what exactly was said, which day, in whose tone. Your Moon tends to skip straight to the philosophy, everything happens for a reason, it'll all work out, and some feelings need the particulars before they'll settle. When they don't get them they come back as restlessness, a sudden urge to book a flight or quit something.

With a partner this looks like being cheerful about a problem that's actually bothering you, and wanting space the moment the conversation gets detailed. With friends it's being the one who's always up for an adventure and hard to reach when things are dull or sad. The body shows it as a need to move, to walk it off. So walk it off. On the way back, name the specific moment that set you off, with as much detail as you can remember.
moon.reversed:
The reversed Magician on a Sagittarius Moon tends to preach to itself. Mercury in detriment, turned inwards, takes a feeling and makes a sermon out of it. You know what you ought to feel, you've got the philosophy ready, and the actual hurt or fear sits there unattended underneath the explanation. Or the restlessness takes over and you keep moving so you never have to look at it.

At home this shows as plans changed at short notice, a lot of fresh starts, and a partner who's tired of never knowing where you'll be. With friends it's the funny version of a bad week, told so well nobody asks how you really are. Before you make the next big change, sit down for ten minutes and say specifically what you're trying to get away from. Say it to someone if you can.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open and friendly, a bit loud, ready for anything, and people like that about you straight away. The Magician on that doorway brings Mercury in detriment, and it's worth knowing what that means for how you come across. Your instinct is to go big, the bold statement, the funny exaggeration, the broad-brush plan, while Mercury wants the right word in the right place. Working against the grain doesn't make you bad at it. It makes it take effort.

The Virgo square adds friction at the start of things. You'd sooner jump in than read the terms, and you tend to learn the details after you've said yes. That can be charming. It can also leave you promising the earth at a first meeting and then quietly dreading the follow-up email. The Eight of Wands decan, Mercury's piece of your sign, is the good version of this, energy that gets things moving fast, introductions that turn into projects inside a week. People remember how quickly you got something started, and they'll judge you on whether it got finished.

In a new job it's the energy everyone loves in the first week and the unanswered emails by the sixth. Travelling, it's the booking you made in a hurry that had a condition you didn't read. In a new friendship it's the invitation to something wonderful made on impulse, and the other person waiting to see if you meant it. Before you say yes to the next big thing, ask one practical question. Ask it even if it feels like it spoils the mood a little.
rising.reversed:
Turned upside down on a Sagittarius Ascendant, the card makes first impressions a bit unreliable. The big easy talk that usually opens doors comes out as bluster or tactlessness, and Mercury in detriment blurts the blunt thing in the wrong company. Or you overpromise so warmly that people are let down later by the ordinary reality of what you can do.

At work this looks like the client who remembers what you promised better than you do. Socially it's the joke that went down badly with someone you'd only just met, and the apology you never quite made. Slow the first five minutes down. Ask a question, listen to the whole answer, and promise nothing until the second conversation, however much you'd like to.

sun.upright:
A Capricorn Sun wants to build something that lasts and to be respected for having built it. The Magician comes into your sign as Saturn's guest, with no rank of its own, and it picks up Saturn's seriousness. That's no bad thing. The card's skill turns practical and strategic, the kind of cleverness that knows how a system works and where the lever is. Virgo, Mercury's exalted sign, is trine to Capricorn, earth to earth, so your planning and the card's craft get on well.

Where it gets awkward is the Gemini end. Gemini is quincunx to Capricorn, five signs apart with nothing in common, and it's the part of Mercury that plays, tries things for fun and changes its mind. You don't find that easy. A Capricorn Sun can treat every idea as a commitment, so it doesn't try many, and the ones it does try get carried out properly and a bit joylessly. I've seen a lot of Capricorns who are excellent at their jobs and have forgotten what they'd do if nobody was marking it.

Career-wise, it's the plan that's working and the side idea you dismissed as not serious enough. With money it's being very sensible and slightly afraid of spending on anything that won't pay back. With a parent or someone senior it can be the habit of still trying to earn their approval with results. Give yourself one project with no purpose at all, something small you're allowed to be bad at and nobody gets to see. Put an hour a week into it and don't measure anything.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with The Magician reversed can get calculating. Mercury under Saturn is shrewd, and upside down it starts measuring people for their usefulness, or treating every conversation as a negotiation to be won. The skill's still there. It's just gone cold. Or it goes the other way and the tools stay in the box, because you've decided you're not senior enough or qualified enough yet to use them.

At work it shows as waiting for permission you don't actually need, or taking credit a little too efficiently. At home it's the evening spent answering work email because that feels safer than talking to anyone. With friends it's the catch-up you keep postponing until things calm down. Pick one thing you'd do if you already had the title you're working towards, and go and do it.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safe when things are under control and it's proved it can cope. The Magician brings Mercury in as Saturn's guest, with no special dignity, and it gives you a very practical way of handling feeling. You deal with an emotion by working out what to do about it. That's often wise. The Virgo trine makes it easy, earth to earth, and people come to you in a crisis because you'll have a plan before they've stopped crying.

The Gemini quincunx is where it snags. The lighter end of Mercury, the part that chats, jokes and lets things out, doesn't find much purchase in a Capricorn Moon, so things stay in. You can go a long time without mentioning that you're struggling. You'd sooner handle it yourself. From outside that looks like strength, and partly it is. Carrying it quietly also means nobody's standing there when you reach the end of what you can manage alone, and by then you're usually too proud to ring anyone.

With a partner this is the tired silence after a long week that they read as distance. With a parent it can be the family habit of just getting on with things and not making a fuss. In the body it lands as tension in the shoulders, the jaw, the knees, and sleep that doesn't refresh you. Tell one person one thing you're finding hard, in plain words, without also telling them your plan for fixing it.
moon.reversed:
The Magician reversed on a Capricorn Moon is a mind that won't clock off. Mercury under Saturn turns inwards and becomes a strict supervisor, reviewing your mistakes, rehearsing the difficult meeting, planning for disasters that haven't happened and probably won't. Rest starts to feel like slacking. Feelings get filed under things to deal with later, and later keeps not arriving.

This shows up at home as being there and not there, on the sofa and still at your desk in your head. It shows in sleep as the early waking with a list already running. A partner may have stopped asking what's wrong because the answer is always 'nothing, just busy'. Give yourself one evening this week with nothing productive in it. If you feel guilty, notice the guilt, and stay on the sofa anyway.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising comes across as capable, reserved and older than its years, and people assume you're in charge before you've said so. The Magician on that entrance hands Mercury to Saturn's Ascendant. There's no special dignity in it, but it works. You read as somebody who knows what they're talking about, and with Virgo trine Capricorn the detail backs you up. You arrive prepared and people can tell.

What's harder is the lightness. Capricorn is cardinal and it starts things, but it starts them formally, and the Gemini quincunx means the easy chat and play of this card don't come naturally to your Ascendant. People can find you slightly intimidating at first, and the warmth you've got takes a while to show. The Magician begins with the tools out on the table, and you'd prefer to begin with your credentials. A bit of informality would often get you further, and faster, and you know that and still find it hard.

At a job interview all this goes very well. On a first date it can make the date feel like a job interview. In a new neighbourhood it's being respected and not invited round. With a new team it's being trusted with the budget in the first week and left out of the pub on Friday. At the next thing you walk into, lead with a question about the other person's week or a small joke at your own expense. Save the credentials for when someone asks.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising with this card reversed can look cold at first contact. Mercury under Saturn turns cautious and clipped, and you come across as guarded, or as quietly sizing people up. Or you overprepare so thoroughly that the first meeting goes stiff, as if you're reading from a script in your head and can't go off it.

In work it's the new colleague who's a bit frightened of you and won't bring you their questions. In dating it's being interesting and hard to get close to, and the other person deciding it isn't worth the effort. At the next introduction, admit to something you don't know, a small gap, owned without fuss. Then ask the other person to explain it to you.

sun.upright:
An Aquarius Sun wants to see how things could be better and to be recognised for thinking differently. The Magician is a guest in your sign, with no special rank, and it takes its colour from Saturn, your traditional ruler, or Uranus if you work with the modern one. Gemini is trine to Aquarius, air to air, so the card's quick mind sits easily with yours. Ideas come to you fast and often from odd angles. You connect things other people keep in separate boxes.

The strain is between the idea and the doing. Aquarius is fixed air, it holds a belief for a long time, and the card asks you to put that belief into your hands. Virgo, Mercury's exalted sign, is quincunx to Aquarius, five signs apart with nothing in common, and that's the gap between your theory and the fiddly business of making it happen. You'll know the feeling of explaining a brilliant system and being faintly bored by the thought of building it. Mercury also rules the middle decan of Aquarius, the Six of Swords, a card of crossing to calmer water, so the ideas worth following are the ones that actually move you somewhere.

You'll recognise it at work in suggestions of yours that are ahead of their time and still sitting in a document, and I'd guess there's more than one. In a friendship group it's having a theory about everyone's problems and less to say about your own. In a community project it's the vision that needs somebody to draw up the rota. Choose one idea and give it a practical first step that involves another person. Send them the message that gets it going.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, an Aquarius Sun can get stuck being clever. Mercury under Saturn goes rigid and sure of itself, and fixed air holds a position long after the argument's been won or lost. You're right, possibly, and nobody's listening, and you're a little proud of that. Or the ideas stay locked in your head because you've decided people wouldn't get them anyway.

In work it shows as the argument you keep having with your manager about the same system, word for word. With friends it's being detached and interesting when someone needed you to be warm and ordinary. At home it's winning the debate and losing the evening. Find one person who disagrees with you and ask them to explain their view until you could argue it yourself.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs a bit of distance from its own feelings. You process by stepping back, looking at the situation from above and working out what's really going on. The Magician brings Mercury in as Saturn's guest, and with Gemini trine Aquarius, air to air, that comes naturally. Words help you. Understanding helps. Friends help most of all, especially the ones you can talk to about ideas as well as feelings.

The difficulty is that understanding a feeling from above isn't the same as having it. The Virgo quincunx points at the body, the practical, messy side of emotion, and that's the part you tend to skip. You can analyse your own sadness very clearly and still have it sitting in your chest a week later. People close to you might find you calm to the point of seeming far away, and you might find their emotional need a bit much, which you'd never say. Some things have to be felt in the body before any explanation will stick, and fixed air can hold off that moment for a surprisingly long time.

With a partner it's the calm discussion of a problem that leaves them feeling you weren't really in the room. With friends it's being the one everyone rings for advice and not quite knowing who you'd ring yourself. In the body it's a tension across the chest or shoulders that doesn't leave. When a feeling comes up, put a hand on the place you feel it and stay there for a minute before you work anything out.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on an Aquarius Moon, The Magician can overthink until nothing's felt at all. Mercury under Saturn turns inwards and builds theories about your own mood. You're detached, you're analytical, and you're lonely in a way that's hard to put into words. Or the mind jumps restlessly between causes, group chats and projects, anything to avoid the one feeling that's sitting there waiting.

It tends to show up as a partner saying they can't reach you, or friends who only ever see the bright, interesting version of you. Sleep may turn light and broken. Say one feeling to one person using the plainest word you can find, sad or scared or lonely, and don't add an explanation after it. Let them respond before you say anything else.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as friendly, a bit unusual and hard to predict. People can tell you're thinking about something interesting and they'd like to know what. The Magician on your Ascendant brings Mercury in as a guest coloured by Saturn, with Gemini trine to Aquarius, so the card's quickness comes out as original conversation and ideas people haven't heard before. First meetings with you tend to be memorable.

What pulls against it is fixed air's habit of holding a position. You'll walk in with a strong view, and this card is about using the tools actually on the table, which means adapting to whoever's there. The Virgo quincunx adds friction with the practical side. You can make a fantastic first impression with an idea and a much vaguer one when someone asks how it would work. And there's the detachment. People sense you're friendly and slightly out of reach in the same moment, and they're not sure which one to believe.

In work it's the interview where you gave the most original answer and they hired someone safer. In a friendship it's being liked by many and known well by very few. In dating it's the fascinating first evening and the other person going home unsure whether you were interested at all. At the next first meeting, let them see one thing you care about and tell them why it matters to you.
rising.reversed:
The card reversed on an Aquarius Ascendant can make you come across as contrary. Mercury under Saturn, upside down, argues for the sake of it or stays so detached that people can't tell what you think of them. It can read as arrogance when it's really discomfort with the small talk and the not knowing anyone.

At work that's the meeting where you disagreed with everything and nobody could tell what you'd propose instead. Socially it's being the odd one out on purpose and then wondering why you feel left out. With a new neighbour it's being perfectly civil and completely unknowable. Pick one ordinary thing to agree with, sincerely, in your next conversation with someone new.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns want to feel connected to something bigger, and to be known for their imagination and their kindness. The Magician is as far from home in your sign as it ever gets. Mercury is in both detriment and fall in Pisces, which means its usual method, sort it, name it, get it done, simply doesn't work here. It has to learn your sign's way of knowing, which is by feel, by image, by a sense of what's right before you can say why.

This isn't bad news, though it can feel like it. Virgo, Mercury's exalted sign, sits opposite Pisces, and an opposition is the same axis seen from the other end. Virgo is the list, Pisces is the dream, and the card is asking you to bring something from one side across to the other. Gemini squares Pisces as well, which adds friction. You'll feel it as scattered attention, a lot of beginnings and a vague sense of having lost the thread. Your gifts are real, they just don't arrive in a sensible order, and what's asked is that you hold one of them long enough to make it solid.

On the job, it's the creative mind whose best idea turns up in the shower and never makes it to the meeting. In love it's the partner who understands without words and struggles to say what they themselves need. With money it's a sense that it'll all be fine, which sometimes it isn't. Keep a small notebook near your bed or in your pocket for a month. Write down one idea a day, and at the end of the month pick one to start.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card reversed can drift. Mercury in detriment and fall, turned over, loses the thread entirely, and the skill you have goes into escape. Daydreams, other people's problems, a series on the laptop, anything but your own plans. Or it goes into telling people what they want to hear, which Pisces can do beautifully and which leaves you worn out and slightly lost.

At work it shows up as missed deadlines you feel terrible about and can't quite explain. In relationships it's agreeing to things and then quietly not doing them. With your own creative work it's the file you haven't opened since the start of the year. Choose one small promise to yourself and keep it every day for a week, something tiny like a ten-minute walk. Tick it off on paper each time you do it.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon feels what everyone in the room feels and often can't tell whose feeling it is. What you need is quiet, softness and time alone for the water to settle. The Magician comes in at its weakest here, with Mercury in detriment and fall. The card's planet has to give up on logic and learn to listen, and that suits you better than it sounds, because your feelings don't come as sentences. They come as moods, pictures and dreams.

The trouble is the Virgo opposition. Some part of you wants to sort it all out, to have a clear explanation, and often there isn't one. You can spend hours trying to work out why you're sad and end up more confused than when you started. Gemini squares Pisces too, and that's the mind racing, reading far too much into a text, flicking from worry to worry. The card asks you to find words anyway, imperfect ones if need be, because what goes unsaid in a water sign tends to pool and go stale.

With a partner it looks like soaking up their mood and thinking it's yours. With friends it's being everyone's listener and nobody's confidant.
